headline: SQLite is being rewritten in Rust to modernize the "most reliable" embedded database
summary: Developers are exploring a Rust-based alternative to SQLite, aiming for 100% compatibility while adding modern features like concurrent writes, async I/O, and native vector search for AI-driven applications.
details: SQLite is an embedded database library, not a server, reading and writing to a single disk file. Its simplicity makes it a silent foundation of modern computing, used in browsers, smartphones, desktop apps, and IoT devices.

An ambitious project is underway to rewrite SQLite from scratch in Rust, aiming for 100% compatibility while introducing modern capabilities. This initiative addresses practical limitations emerging in many contemporary applications.

While SQLite is robust due to its conservative and minimalist design, its maintenance model is atypical for open-source. Evolution is guided by a few individuals, limiting external contributions and the rapid integration of new features like advanced concurrency or non-blocking I/O.

The goal is to build an alternative that maintains SQLite's compatibility but can evolve with different priorities. Key requirements include absolute data integrity and allowing users to replace SQLite with the new implementation without rewriting their applications.

One historical limitation of SQLite is its single-writer model, where only one writer can access the database at a time. The Rust alternative aims to allow multiple simultaneous writes on different data portions, resolving conflicts only when operations touch the same rows.

SQLite typically performs blocking disk I/O, meaning the thread waits during read or write operations. Modern architectures, especially those with async runtimes, benefit from non-blocking I/O, which allows the thread to yield control during I/O operations, improving responsiveness and resource utilization.

The rise of AI has introduced a new requirement: efficient storage and rapid searching of embeddings. The Rust implementation seeks to integrate native vector types and indices, allowing embeddings and relational data to reside in a single file with a unified SQL interface.

Building a reliable database is challenging; adding features is comparatively easier. The project emphasizes rigorous testing, including deterministic simulation, to ensure the new database never compromises data integrity, even under adverse conditions.

headline_marked: [[20 Claude agents for M&A diligence]] built on one rule: cite the source or cut the claim
headline: 20 Claude agents for M&A diligence built on one rule: cite the source or cut the claim
summary: This MIT-licensed, open-source project called 'The Deal Team' uses specialized AI agents to verify every factual claim against source documents, preventing costly errors in deal pricing.
details: Introducing 'The Deal Team', an MIT-licensed, free, and open-source project on GitHub. It comprises 20 specialized Claude agents designed for M&A diligence, built on the principle: every claim must be cited to its source, or it is cut.

In M&A, inaccurate AI summaries can be disastrous. An invented EBITDA figure or a softened risk assessment can form the basis of a deal, leading to significant financial losses and damaged credibility before the error is discovered.

Unlike a single large AI model that provides confident but untraceable summaries, 'The Deal Team' uses twenty small agents. Each agent has a specific job, is built to show its work, and traces every factual claim back to its original document.

A sample brief for 'Project Sentinel', a synthetic target, demonstrates the system's power. It caught a contradiction where one page of a Confidential Information Memorandum (CIM) stated customer diversification, while another listed accounts showing a top customer at 22% of revenue. The brief presents both passages verbatim, cited to their pages, allowing human analysts to make the informed call.

The system also features a 'discard log' for unverifiable claims. For instance, claims like 'the company has no outstanding litigation' or 'technician retention is strong' are cut if not supported by documents, transforming them into actionable questions for further due diligence.

The core philosophy is transparent: a verified claim shows its source, a contradiction shows both sides, and an unverifiable claim never reaches the user, instead becoming a prompt for investigation. This ensures trust and accuracy in critical financial decisions.

Users can interact with the agents by copy-pasting prompts into claude.ai or installing them as Claude skills. Each agent is a self-contained SKILL.md with a copy-ready prompt, streamlining integration into existing workflows.

The crucial habit is to always check the source of any important number. The agents are engineered to facilitate this check quickly, clearly indicating where each claim originated and highlighting when necessary information was missing rather than fabricating it.
